name: Dusty aubergine
lede: Dusty aubergine is a very dark, muted purple, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Kokimurasaki, literally "deep purple," with no vegetable in its original name at all.

sections.title: A deep purple, not a vegetable
sections.body:
Kokimurasaki (深紫) is named in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors simply for being a deep purple, *murasaki*, rather than for the aubergine (eggplant) the English rendering here suggests [1]. The page gives no further history for the name beyond that literal meaning, and it is undocumented in the sources consulted here [1].

Its nearest named neighbor on file is [[romanesque]], 2.8 units off, close enough on screen to read as the same color [2]; [[dark-purple]] sits 3.6 off [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within six units of this swatch in 52 of 23,781 paintings, 0.22 percent, as photographed; looking inside each painting for at least five percent coverage narrows that to 34 [3]. That makes it rarer than 55 percent of the named colors in our library [3]. It peaks in the 1500s, present in 0.4 percent of our 2,231 paintings from that century, 1.9 times the museums' baseline rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a hidden color, in 41 percent of its 34 appearances by lightness rank [3].

The earliest match, by Ambrogio Lorenzetti, dates to 1342, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [3].

questions.q: True or false: the Japanese name for this color refers to a vegetable.

openers: The English name says aubergine; the Japanese name just says deep purple.
